cancellation.sec: TERMINATION OF COVERAGE / Termination of Plan Membership (p.10-11)
cancellation.v: TERMINATION OF COVERAGE Termination of Plan Membership : A Plan Member’s coverage will terminate with the Plan for any one of the reasons outlined in this section. This termination language will apply to each class of eligible Members. Coverage ends on the last day of the month following one of the events listed, unless otherwise specified. Spouse and dependent children will terminate on the same date as the Member for the all benefits; or for a dependent child, the end of the month in which they turn 26. 1. Working owner does not maintain good standing by completing all required activities each year. 2. Voluntary Termination of Coverage. Coverage will end on the last day for which a contribution has been paid for a Plan Member who voluntarily ends cover age. 3. Death. Coverage will end on the date of death of the member. 4. Contributions. If the covered Plan Member or beneficiary fails to remit required contributions within thirty (30) days when such payment is due, then coverage will terminate at the end of the period for which a contribution is made. 5. Military Duty. The date the Plan Member becomes a full-time member of the Armed Forces of any United States on a full-time active-duty basis, or a government unit covered by or Uniformed Services Employment and re- employment Rights Act of 1993 (USERRA). Reserve duty, drills and summer camp shall be excluded from the definition of active duty unless such duty lasts over 30 days as defined by the act. 6. Plan Termination. The date the Plan is terminated. Rescission of Coverage : Coverage under this Plan may be rescinded under certain circumstances. A determination by the Plan that a rescission is warranted will be considered an Adverse Benefit Determination for purposes of review and appeal. A Participant whose coverage is being rescinded will be provided a thirty (30) day notice period as described under Health Care Reform and regulatory guidance. Such notice shall be considered an Adverse Benefit Determination. At the conclusion of the thirty (30) day notice period, coverage shall be terminated retroactive to the date identified in the notification. Claims Incurred after the retroactive date of termination shall not be further processed and/or paid under the Plan. Claims Incurred after the retroactive date of termination that were paid under the Plan will be treated as erroneously paid claims under this Plan.

compliance_risks.could_misstate: Selling TDK from the FirstEnroll brochure and telling a client there is no pre-existing limitation, because the document in front of the agent does not mention one. Also the classic setting-based error - saying the office visit is covered and only the hospital is excluded. The exclusion is CONDITION-based, not setting-based.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Do not say TDK has no pre-existing limitation. Do not say 'the office visit is covered, just not the hospital'. Do not rely on the FirstEnroll brochure's silence as evidence there is no exclusion - silence in marketing material is an omission, not a benefit.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: This plan has a pre-existing condition limitation. For the first 12 months after you enroll, conditions you already have are not covered. There is also a 30-day waiting period before sickness benefits begin.

source.sec: General Exclusions item 74 and page 15 footnotes; absence verified across all 18 pages of source 24

compliance_risks.verified_fact: The NEO-channel TDK plan document states the plan does not cover pre-existing conditions for the first 12 months after enrollment, and that all sickness benefits are subject to a 30-day waiting period. The FirstEnroll-channel brochure, which is the document that channel links, contains NO pre-existing condition language at all and no waiting period.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: Always, and the plan-year question must be resolved first - the pre-existing language sits in a document with an April 1 2024 plan year while the brochure claims April 1 2025. Confirm with Detego Health whether it remains in force before quoting the 12-month figure.

compliance_risks.could_misstate: Framing 'no deductible' as generous without disclosing there is also no cap on what the client can spend. The Master Compliance Key requires any no-deductible claim to be paired with disclosure of benefit caps.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Do not say 'no deductible' without immediately disclosing the absence of an out-of-pocket maximum. Do not use any 'the most you'll pay' framing - there is no aggregate cap of any kind on this product.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: There is no deductible on this plan. You should also know there is no out-of-pocket maximum - the plan pays fixed amounts per service, and anything above those amounts is yours. For example inpatient hospitalization pays $1,000 a day up to $15,000 a year.

source.sec: Section V; corroborated by source 24 page 14

compliance_risks.verified_fact: The plan is a limited benefit plan with NO out-of-pocket maximum. Both channel documents agree. There is no deductible either.

compliance_risks.could_misstate: Selling TDK from the FirstEnroll brochure and telling a client there is no pre-existing limitation. The brochure's silence is an omission, not a benefit. This is now confirmed against a CURRENT source, so the 'the SPD is just old' defence no longer applies.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Do not say TDK has no pre-existing limitation. Do not rely on the FirstEnroll brochure's silence. Do not state the scope of the limitation - whether it applies to all benefits or only hospitalization - until C-010 is resolved.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: This plan has a pre-existing condition limitation of 12 months and a 30-day waiting period before sickness benefits begin. I want to confirm exactly which benefits the pre-existing limitation touches before I go further, because the plan documents describe its scope two different ways.

source.sec: TDK Plan 3) and source 27 (NEO plan document); absence verified across all 18 pages of source 24

compliance_risks.verified_fact: CONFIRMED CURRENT. The live NEO portal page for TDK 3 states a pre-existing condition limitation under which hospitalization-related benefits are not payable for the first 12 months, and a 30-day waiting period on sickness benefits. Two independent NEO sources - the 2024 plan document and the 2026 portal page - disclose both. The FirstEnroll-linked brochure discloses neither.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: Always. And note the scope question in C-010 must be settled first: if the limitation is genuinely hospitalization-scoped then 'the office visit is covered, just not the hospital' is ACCURATE for TDK, which is the exact phrasing the playbook flags as a misrepresentation on STM products. An agent could be corrected into the wrong answer.

compliance_risks.could_misstate: Classifying any product from its name. Doing so produces errors in both directions - calling insurance a membership, and calling a service a discount.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Never type or describe a product from its name. Read the Info page.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: Nothing client-facing. This is an internal rule.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: Product names in this portfolio are unreliable indicators of product type IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. 'AWA SimpleShield Membership Plan' is fixed indemnity insurance. 'Prime Health Pass Discount' is described on its own page as a Diagnostic Services Product delivering services. Between April and September NEO inserted the word 'Membership' into four Safe Guard product names without any evident change of type. Meanwhile 'AssistPro Discount' genuinely is a discount program.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: Before any add-on is described on a call, and before any tooling assigns it a category.

compliance_risks.could_misstate: Selling TDK's preventive care as a headline benefit without the hospital carve-out - a client who has a covered screening done at a hospital gets nothing. And selling it without mentioning an ongoing participation requirement the member is expected to meet.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Do not present preventive care on TDK without the hospital exclusion. Do not omit the activity requirement at point of sale.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: Preventive services are covered, but not if they're done at a hospital - it needs to be a physician's office or clinic. And as part of this plan you're expected to complete around eight short wellness activities a year; some are required.

source.sec: Preventative Health Services slides and 'Activities for Working Owners' slide

compliance_risks.verified_fact: TWO material items exist only in TDK training: preventive health services are NOT covered if provided at a hospital; and enrollees are expected to complete an average of 8 wellness activities every 12 months, some mandatory, with biometric and DNA screenings at additional cost.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: Every TDK call. Note both facts are rank-6 training-only and cannot yet be stated as contractual - confirm against the plan document first.

compliance_risks.could_misstate: Nothing directly - this is a defect in the document, not in what the agent says. But it means the clause telling the client who to contact about claims may be unreadable, and the client may later say they were never told who their agent was.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Do not tell a client the agreement names their agent.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: Give the client your own name, agency and email verbally on the recorded call, and confirm you are their contact for benefit and claims questions. Do not rely on the agreement to have done it.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: The FirstEnroll enrollment-agreement template served on the live storefront contains unrendered variables - $parentcompany, $product_label, $agent_fullname, $agent_Email, $parentemail - confirmed on two unrelated product families (American Financial Critical Illness page 38175, and Health Choice Silver page 32339). The affected clauses are the third-party administrator disclaimer, the Plan and Claims Inquiries clause and the Writing Agent Contact block.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: Raise with FirstEnroll whether the executed enrollment document renders these variables. See G-039.

compliance_risks.could_misstate: The scope. Because the limitation attaches to the hospitalization confinement component, saying 'the office visit is covered, just not the hospital' is closer to accurate for TDK than for an STM - but the preventive and physician components carry their own separate 30-day waiting period, so 'covered' is still wrong in the first thirty days. Both facts have to be said together.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Do not say there is no pre-existing limitation because the brochure does not mention one. Do not say benefits start immediately.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: There is a thirty-day waiting period before benefits can be used, apart from the virtual doctor service and emergencies. And the hospital confinement benefit will not pay for anything you were advised about, treated for, or had symptoms of in the twelve months before your start date, for your first twelve months on the plan.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: REVISION OF K-003. The FirstEnroll enrollment TERMS panel on the TDK product page DOES disclose the 12-month pre-existing limitation and the 30-day sickness waiting period. TDK_Promo_Combined.pdf, the brochure linked from the same page, discloses neither. The pre-existing limitation is scoped to the supplemental hospitalization confinement benefit component, with a full prudent-person definition, 12-month lookback, applying for the first 12 months.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: This resolves the scope half of C-010 in favour of the hospitalization-scoped reading. The 2024 plan document's general-exclusion item 74 still needs reconciling, and the TDK 2025-26 SPD is still outstanding.

compliance_risks.could_misstate: Telling a caller the plan includes prescription access without saying specialty drugs are excluded. Anyone on an injectable or infused medication - which includes many common autoimmune, oncology and diabetes therapies - is materially affected, and the exclusion appears in no brochure or portal page.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Do not describe TDK as including prescription coverage without the specialty exclusion in the same sentence. Do not attempt to list which drugs count - the definition is deliberately broad and no formulary is held.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: The plan has a limited prescription formulary through the virtual doctor service, and it specifically excludes specialty medications - broadly, high-cost drugs, biologics, and anything injected or infused. If you take anything like that, this plan will not cover it.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: 'This plan specifically excludes all specialty medications, including human growth hormones.' Specialty medications are defined broadly as high-cost, high complexity and/or high touch, often biologics, injectable or infused, some oral. The plan includes only a limited formulary through MyLiveDoc.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: Ask the caller what they take before quoting. See G-045 - the formulary itself is not held.

compliance_risks.could_misstate: Presenting TDK as a health plan purchase. It is a Working Owner enrollment with data-contribution obligations, a tax document, and a state bar delivered as a client attestation rather than a system check.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Do not skip the Working Owner model. Do not characterise the Preferred Units in any way - see C-018. Do not proceed without establishing the caller's state of residence.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: To be eligible you join Healthcare Data Analytics as a working owner. You will be asked to complete around eight to ten health data activities a year, you receive an annual K-1 tax form, and this plan is not available in Oregon, Washington, Vermont or New Hampshire. Which state are you in?
compliance_risks.verified_fact: The TDK enrollee becomes a Working Owner of Healthcare Data Analytics LLC, a Tennessee LLC and subsidiary of Population Science Management USA - the same parent named in the SmartChoice mandatory verification script. Obligations: approximately 8-10 data activities per year, timely response to requests for exchange of health and socioeconomic data, regular communication. The Company may assign projects and may invoke a Call Right forcing the sale of the member's interest. The member is granted three Preferred Units, receives a Guaranteed Payment under IRC 707(c), receives an annual K-1, and arbitrates in Davidson County, Tennessee. The client also attests they do not live in Oregon, Washington, Vermont or New Hampshire.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: SmartChoice has a mandatory recorded verification script for this same model; TDK has none that has been found. See G-046 - that should be escalated.

compliance_risks.could_misstate: Describing TDK as covering care. After this list what remains is office visits, a wellness exam, virtual care through MyLiveDoc, and a per-day hospitalization indemnity. A caller who mentions a bad back, a diabetic supply, an injectable medication, physical therapy or chemotherapy is asking about something the plan excludes by name.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Do not say the plan covers diagnostics, therapy, or medication. Do not describe it as covering an illness - it pays scheduled amounts for scheduled services.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: This plan pays for office visits up to set copays and limits, a wellness exam, virtual doctor visits, and a fixed daily amount if you are admitted to hospital. It does not pay for lab work, x-rays, physical therapy, chiropractic, chemotherapy, ambulance, durable medical equipment or prescription drugs.

source.sec: Section VI (8) sub-exclusions (a)-(gg) and Section VII items 2-7, byte-identical in all five documents

compliance_risks.verified_fact: The TDK Member Plan Summary excludes, by name: chemotherapy and radiation therapy; ambulance; diagnostic x-rays; laboratory studies and diagnostic services; durable medical equipment; injectables; prosthetic devices; orthotic appliances; casts, splints and surgical dressings; physical therapy; occupational therapy; speech therapy; chiropractic and spinal manipulation; pain management; cardiac rehabilitation; genetic tests; infertility treatment; TMJ; diabetic self-management training and diabetic shoes; allergy testing and injections; contraception; reconstructive surgery; mental health and substance abuse treatment; and prescription drugs. It also excludes acupuncture, abortion, adoption expenses and alternative medicine.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: Ask the caller what care they actually expect to use before quoting. See K-042 for the separate specialty-medication exclusion in the enrollment agreement, which does not appear in these plan summaries at all.

compliance_risks.could_misstate: Anything sourced to this document alone. The practical risk is quoting a benefit the document elsewhere denies, or being unable to substantiate a statement if a claim is disputed.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Do not tell a client the plan summary sets out their benefits clearly. Do not answer a maternity question, a dependent-age question for a 25-year-old, or a 'what counts as pre-existing' question from this document.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: Quote from the Schedule of Benefits, which agrees with the portal, the enrollment agreement and the training material on the co-pays and the hospitalization benefit. State the 30-day waiting period and the 12-month pre-existing limitation every time.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: The governing Member Plan Summary contradicts itself on four things an agent will be asked about on every call: it says 'There are no co-pays benefits in this Plan' and then schedules $25/$50 or $50/$75 co-pays; it says 'Hospital Care is not covered under the Plan' and 'This Plan does not include any hospitalization benefits' and then pays $1,000-$1,500 per day for hospitalization; it excludes ambulance and schedules an ambulance benefit on TDK 4 and 5; and it gives three different answers on maternity. It also defines 'Pre-Existing Condition' nowhere while pointing twice to a Defined Terms section that does not exist.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: See C-038 through C-042 and G-060, G-061. The full defect list should go to Detego Health.

compliance_risks.could_misstate: Carrying a surgery or emergency room benefit from TDK 4 or 5 onto TDK 1, 2 or 3 - the five plans look like a simple ladder and are usually described as one, so the temptation is to assume the cheaper plans have the same categories at lower amounts. They do not have those categories at all.
compliance_risks.do_not_say: Do not quote a surgery, emergency room or ambulance amount on TDK 1, 2 or 3. On TDK 4 and 5 never quote the emergency room or ambulance amount without 'if admitted'.
compliance_risks.safe_wording: On plans one, two and three the benefits are office visits, wellness, virtual care and a daily hospital amount. Surgery and emergency room benefits start at plan four.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: TDK 4 and TDK 5 contain three benefit categories that TDK 1, 2 and 3 do not have at all: In/Out-patient Surgery, Emergency Room (if admitted) and Ambulance Benefit (if admitted). These lines are NOT PRESENT in the TDK 1, 2 or 3 Schedule of Benefits in either the plan summary or the portal.
compliance_risks.verify_before_saying: The ambulance line on TDK 4 and 5 is contradicted by sub-exclusion (a) - see C-041.

compliance_risks.do_not_say: For any product in this group, do not answer a coverage, exclusion, waiting-period or pre-existing question on a recorded call from portal material alone. Obtain the carrier document first.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: 51 of the 80 products on the NEO agent storefront have no brochure, certificate or policy document attached anywhere in the enrolment system. For those products the NEO reference page is the only available source, and four of those pages carry a limitations or exclusions heading with no text beneath it.

compliance_risks.do_not_say: The monthly cost quoted on a recorded call must include this fee, or the fee must be stated separately before the payment authorisation. Quoting the product page price alone understates what the client will be charged.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: A 3.5% credit-card or ACH processing fee applies to every payment and appears only in the platform TERMS panel, which more than half the product pages do not display at all.

compliance_risks.do_not_say: Do not tell a client a scheduled benefit amount will be paid in full without qualifying it by the URC limit.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: A platform-level usual, reasonable and customary cap applies on top of every product's stated benefits and appears only in the TERMS panel.

compliance_risks.do_not_say: Every recorded verification must cover all four elements. Omitting the recurring monthly amount or the automatic draft is a breach of the platform agreement, not only a compliance risk.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: The platform agreement requires an electronic signature or a recorded verification script with every sale, and specifies the four things the member must be shown to understand: the product, its benefits, the initial payment, and the recurring monthly amount drafted automatically.

compliance_risks.do_not_say: Disclose to any client on a tight account that a single failed draft can end the plan.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: A dishonoured payment can result in forfeiture of the plan with no liability on anyone's part, expressly including where the dishonour was inadvertent or without cause.

compliance_risks.do_not_say: Never describe NEO as the insurance company. Name the carrier for the specific product.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: Neo Insurance Solutions is an agency and platform, not the insurer, and disclaims liability for agents' conduct and representations.

compliance_risks.do_not_say: Disclose the 3.5% card/ACH processing fee on every sale regardless of which page the client was shown. Do not rely on the panel a given product page happens to display.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: The storefront serves two different versions of the NEO enrolment agreement. The shorter one, on the MDLive pages, omits the 3.5% processing fee, the contact and electronic-document consents, the HIPAA statement and the member signature block.

compliance_risks.do_not_say: Do not tell a client 'the terms are on the page'. Establish which agreement governs their enrolment, and disclose the 3.5% processing fee regardless of which panel their product displays.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: Four different NEO enrolment agreements are in simultaneous circulation on the storefront, and most product pages show none at all.

compliance_risks.do_not_say: Until the PDFs are filed, any compliance challenge to a benefit statement on these products can be answered only with the ledger's citations, not with the underlying document. Treat filing them as outstanding remediation, not housekeeping.
compliance_risks.verified_fact: Ten of the eleven linked brochures are READ and fully extracted into the ledger, but the PDF files themselves are not in Drive. The documents behind 25 live variants therefore exist in this project only as extracted facts, not as retrievable source documents.

excluded_services.v: VII. GENERAL EXCLUSIONS AND LIMITATIONS 1. No payment will be eligible under any portion of this Plan for expenses Incurred by a Covered Person for the expenses or circumstances listed below. If an expense is paid that is found to be excluded or limited as shown below, the Plan has the right to collect that amount from the payee, the Covered Person or from future benefits and any such payment does not waive the written exclusions, limitations or other terms of the Plan. Limitations listed can be informed in the Medical Benefits Section. 2. Abortion will not be considered eligible. 3. Acupuncture will not be considered eligible. 4. Adoption expenses will not be considered eligible. 5. Alcohol services, supplies, care or treatment to a Covered Person for an Injury or Sickness which occurred as a result of that Covered Person’s illegal use of alcohol. 6. Allergy testing/injections will not be considered eligible. 7. Alternative Medicine or Complementary Medicine services and supplies related to alternative or complementary medicine, including but not limited to acupressure, acupuncture, aroma therapy, bioenergial synchronization technique (BEST), contact reflex analysis, holistic medicine herbal therapy, hypnotism, iridology (study of the iris), naturopathy, Reiki therapy, Rolfing, thermography, or other forms of alternative treatment as defined by the National Center for Complementary and Alternative Medicine of the National Institutes of Health or any similar or successor organization. 8. Ambulance Services – Ground / Air is limited, see Summary of Benefits Page. 9. Autism Services (Inpatient and Outpatient) will not be considered eligible. 10. Autopsy expenses will not be considered eligible. 11. Autotransfusions charges or cell saver transfusions occurring during or after surgery will not be considered eligible. 12. Biofeedback. 13. Blood or Other Body Tissue and Fluids, Including Storage will not be considered eligible. 14. Cardiac Rehabilitation will not be considered eligible. 15. Chemotherapy / Radiation Therapy will not be considered eligible. 16. Chiropractic Services will not be considered eligible. 17. Close Relative expenses for services, care or supplies provided by a person who normally resides in the Covered Person’s home or by a Close Relative will not be considered eligible. 18. Complications services or treatment required as a result of complications from a treatment or procedure not covered under the Plan will not be considered eligible. 19. Contraceptives expenses (including placement and removal) will not be considered eligible, except as otherwise covered as a preventive service under the Schedule of Benefits and Medical Covered Charges section of the Plan. 20. Convenience Items expenses (personal hygiene and convenience) will not be considered eligible. 21. Cosmetic/Reconstructive Procedures expenses will not be considered eligible. 22. Counseling expenses for religious, marital, or relationship counseling will not be considered eligible. 23. Custodial Care expenses will not be considered eligible. 24. Dental Care expenses incurred in connection with dental care, treatment, x-rays, general anesthesia or Hospital expenses will not be considered eligible. 25. Developmental Delays expenses, including, but not limited to speech therapy, occupational therapy, physical therapy and any related diagnostic testing will not be considered eligible. This exclusion will not apply to expenses related to the diagnosis, testing and treatment of autism, ADD or ADHD and to expenses covered as a preventive service under the Schedule of Benefits and Medical Covered Charges section of the Plan. 26. Diagnostic Testing will not be considered eligible. 27. Dialysis will not be considered eligible. 28. Durable Medical Equipment will not be considered eligible. 29. Employment, Insurance, or License related care - physical exams or immunizations, or any other treatment required for enrollment in any insurance program, as a condition of employment, for licensing, or other similar purposes. 30. Exercise Programs will not be considered eligible. 31. Experimental and/or Investigational expenses for treatment, procedures, devices, drugs or medicines which are determined to be Experimental and/or Investigational will not be considered eligible. 32. Eye care - Radial keratotomy, Lasik surgery or other eye surgery to correct vision problems that are alternately correctable by vision lenses. Also, routine eye examinations, including refractions, lenses for the eyes and exams for their fitting (unless specified in the Schedule of Benefits). This exclusion does not apply to aphakic patients and soft lenses or sclera shells intended for use as corneal bandages or as may be covered under the well adult or well child sections of this Plan. 33. Foot Care expenses for routine foot care, treatment of weak, unstable or flat feet will not be considered eligible. 34. Genetic Testing will not be considered eligible. 35. Governmental Agency expenses for services and supplies which are provided by any governmental agency for which the Covered Person is not liable for payment will not be considered eligible. In the case of a state sponsored medical assistance program, benefits payable under this Plan will be primary. Benefits payable under this Plan will also be primary for any Covered Person eligible under TRICARE (the government sponsored program for military dependents). 36. Hair Loss/transplants expenses will not be considered eligible. 37. Hazardous Hobby expenses for any condition, Illness or Injury, or complication thereof, arising out of engaging in a hazardous hobby or activity will not be considered eligible. For the purposes of this Plan, “hazardous hobby or activity” is defined as an unusual activity characterized by a constant threat of danger, such as skydiving, auto racing, hang gliding, bungee jumping, and jet ski operating. This does not include common recreational activities, such as water or snow skiing, horseback riding, boating, motorcycling, snowmobiling, all-terrain vehicle riding and team sports. 38. Hearing Exams/Aids expenses for routine hearing examinations, hearing aids (including the fitting thereof) and supplies will not be considered eligible, except as otherwise covered as a preventive service under the Schedule of Benefits and Medical Covered Charges section of the Plan. 39. Home Health Care will not be considered eligible. 40. Homeopathic Treatment expenses for naturopathic and homeopathic treatments, services and supplies will not be considered eligible. 41. Hospice Care will not be considered eligible. 42. Hypnotherapy expenses will not be considered eligible. 43. Illegal acts - charges for services received as a result of Injury or Sickness occurring directly or indirectly, as a result of an Illegal Act, or a riot, or public disturbance. For purposes of this exclusion, the term Illegal Act shall mean any act or series of acts that, if charged, prosecuted and convicted of a criminal offense, a sentence to a term of imprisonment in excess of one year could be imposed. 44. Illegal Occupation/Felony expenses for or in connection with an Injury or Illness arising out of an illegal occupation or commission of a felony will not be considered eligible. 45. Implantable Devices will not be considered eligible. 46. Infertility expenses for confinement, treatment, testing or services related to infertility (the inability to conceive) or the promotion of conception will not be considered eligible unless otherwise indicated in the Schedule of Benefits. Nothing in this section is intended to exclude coverage for any infertility counseling or treatment required to be covered (if any) as a preventive service under the guidelines published by the Health Resources and Services Administration on August 1, 2011 (or any applicable subsequent guidelines). 47. Late submission charges for care, treatment, services or supplies which were incurred more than 12 months prior to the date the charges were submitted to the Plan for payments will not be considered eligible. 48. Maintenance Therapy expenses for Maintenance Therapy of any type when the individual has reached the maximum level of improvement will not be considered eligible. 49. Massage Therapy expenses will not be considered eligible. 50. Maternity/Pregnancy Services will not be considered eligible. 51. Medically Necessary expenses will not be considered eligible. 52. Mental Health Services (Inpatient and Outpatient) will not be considered eligible. 53. Missed Appointments expenses for completion of claim forms, missed appointments or telephone consultations will not be considered eligible. 54. Motor vehicle injury charges incurred for the care or treatment of any injury sustained as a result of or related to any motor vehicle accident to the extent that such care or treatment for that injury is covered by any plan, program, policy or other arrangement providing insurance coverage for vehicles. 55. Negligence expenses for Injuries resulting from negligence, misfeasance, malfeasance, nonfeasance or malpractice on the part of any licensed Physician will not be considered eligible. 56. Never Events expenses for serious preventable adverse events (“Never Events”) will not, in any event, be considered eligible. These Never Events include: a. Surgery performed on the wrong body part; b. Surgery performed on the wrong patient; c. Wrong Surgical procedure performed on a patient; d. Unintentional retention of a foreign object in a patient after Surgery or other procedure; e. Inoperative or immediate postoperative death in an ASA Class I patient; f. Patient death or serious disability associated with the use of contaminated Drugs, devices, or biologics provided by the healthcare facility; g. Patient death or serious disability associated with the use or function of a device in a patient in which the device is used for functions other than as intended; h. Patient death or serious disability associated with intravascular air embolism that occurs while being cared for in a healthcare facility; i. Patient death or serious disability associated with patient leaving the facility without permission; j. Infant discharged to the wrong person; k. Patient death or serious disability associated with a medication error (e.g., error involving the wrong drug, wrong dose, wrong patient, wrong time, wrong rate, wrong preparations, or wrong route of administration); l. Patient death or serious disability associated with a hemolytic reaction due to the administration of ABO- incompatible blood or blood products; m. Maternal death or serious disability associated with labor and delivery in a low-risk Pregnancy while being cared for in a healthcare facility; n. Patient death or serious disability associated with hypoglycemia, the onset of which occurs while the patient is being cared for in a healthcare facility; o. Death or serious disability associated with failure to identify and treat hyperbilirubinemia (condition where there is a high amount of bilirubin in the blood) in newborns; p. Stage 3 or 4 pressure ulcers acquired after admission to a healthcare facility; q. Patient death or serious disability due to spinal manipulative therapy; r. Artificial insemination with the wrong donor sperm or wrong egg; s. Patient death or serious disability associated with an electric shock while being cared for in a healthcare facility; t. Any incident in which a line designated for oxygen or other gas to be delivered to a patient contains the wrong gas or is contaminated by toxic substances; u. Patient death or serious disability associated with a burn Incurred from any source while being cared for in a healthcare facility; v. Patient death associated with a fall while being cared for in a healthcare facility; w. Patient death or serious disability associated with the use of restrains or bedrails while being cared for in a healthcare facility; x. Any instance of care ordered by or provided by someone impersonating a Physician, nurse, pharmacist, or other Provider; y. Abduction of a patient of any age; z. Sexual assault on a patient within or on the grounds of a healthcare facility; and a. Death or significant Injury of a patient or staff member resulting from a physical assault (i.e. battery) that occurs within or on the grounds of a healthcare facility. 57. No Legal Obligation expenses for services provided for which the Covered Person has no legal obligation to pay will not be considered eligible. This exclusion will not apply to eligible expenses that may be covered by state Medicaid coverage where federal law requires this Employer’s plan to be primary. 58. Non-Covered Procedures expenses for services related to a non-covered Surgery or procedure will not be considered eligible regardless of when the Surgery or procedure was performed. 59. Not Performed Under the Direction of a Physician expenses for services and supplies which are not prescribed or performed by or under the direction of a Physician will not be considered eligible. 60. Not Recommended by a Physician expenses by a Hospital or covered residential treatment center if hospitalization is not recommended or approved by a legally qualified Physician will not be considered eligible. 61. Nutritional Counseling expenses related to nutritional counseling will not be considered eligible, except as otherwise covered as a preventive service under the Schedule of Benefits and Medical Covered Charges section of the Plan. 62. Nutritional Supplements expenses for nutritional supplements or other enteral supplementation will not be considered eligible, except as specified under Schedule of Benefits and Medical Covered Charges of the Plan. Over-the-counter nutritional supplements or infant formulas will not be considered eligible even if prescribed by a Physician. 63. Obesity - surgical and non-surgical care and treatment of obesity including weight loss or dietary control, whether or not it is in any case a part of a treatment plan for another Illness, will not be considered eligible, except as otherwise covered as a preventive service under the Schedule of Benefits and Medical Covered Charges section of the Plan. 64. Off-label drugs - A charge for FDA-approved drugs that are prescribed for non-FDA-approved uses will not be considered eligible. 65. Office visits , physical examinations, immunizations, and tests when required solely for the following: a. Sports b. Camp c. Employment d. Travel e. Marriage f. Insurance g. Legal Proceedings 66. Operated by the Government expenses for treatment at a facility owned or operated by the government will not be considered eligible, unless the Covered Person is legally obligated to pay. This does not apply to Covered Expenses rendered by a Hospital owned or operated by the United States Veteran’s Administration when services are provided to a Covered Person for a non-service related Illness or Injury. 67. Organ Transplants will not be considered eligible. 68. Outpatient surgery (Facility, Anesthesia and Physician charges) , unless specified in the Schedule of Benefits, will not be considered eligible. 69. Outside the United States (U.S.) expenses for services or supplies if the Covered Person leaves the U.S. or the U.S. Territories for the express purpose of receiving medical treatment will not be considered eligible. 70. Over-the-Counter (OTC) Medication expenses for any over-the-counter medication will not be considered eligible. Expenses for drugs and medicines not requiring a prescription by a licensed Physician and not dispensed by a licensed pharmacist will not be considered eligible, except as otherwise covered as a preventive services under the Schedule of Benefits and Pharmacy Covered Charges section of the Plan. 71. Physical/Speech/Occupational Therapy will not be considered eligible. 72. Plan Allowable Fee expenses in excess of the Plan allowable fee charge will not be considered eligible. 73. Plan Maximums - Charges in excess of Plan maximums will not be considered eligible. 74. Pre-Existing Conditions - This plan does not cover pre-existing conditions for the first 12 months after enrollment. 75. Prenatal/Postnatal Services will not be considered eligible, except as required per ACA guidelines. 76. Prior to Effective Date expenses which are incurred prior to the effective date of your coverage under the Plan will not be considered eligible. 77. Private Duty Nursing expenses for inpatient private duty nursing will not be considered eligible. 78. Prosthetics/Orthotics will not be considered eligible. 79. Pulmonary Rehabilitation will not be considered eligible. 80. Radioactive Contamination expenses Incurred as the result of radioactive contamination or the hazardous properties of nuclear material will not be considered eligible. 81. Radiology (CT, PET, MRI, MRA, SPECT) will not be considered eligible. 82. Recreational and Educational Therapy expenses for recreational and educational services; learning disabilities; behavior modification services; any form of non-medical self-care or self-help training, including any related diagnostic testing; music therapy; health club memberships; aquatic or pool therapies; will not be considered eligible. 83. Refractive Errors expenses for radial keratotomy, Lasik Surgery or any Surgical Procedure to correct refractive errors of the eye will not be considered eligible. 84. Replacement braces - Replacement of braces of the leg, arm, back, neck, or artificial arms or legs, unless there is sufficient change in the Covered Person’s physical condition to make the original device no longer functional, will not be considered eligible. 85. Required by Law - In any case where an individual is required by law to maintain insurance coverage (or to maintain any other security or reserve amount in lieu of insurance coverage), expenses of a Covered Person that would be paid by such insurance coverage are not eligible expenses, regardless of whether the individual is in fact covered under such coverage. For purposes of any required automobile, motorcycle or other vehicle coverage, otherwise eligible expenses below the minimum required coverage or the actual coverage elected, whichever is higher, will be excluded from coverage under this Plan. 86. Riot/Revolt expenses resulting from a Covered Person’s participation in a riot or revolt will not be considered eligible. 87. Safety devices- For drivers and all passengers: charges for the treatment for injuries incurred when not wearing appropriate safety restraints and/or motorcycle helmets, when legally required, will be considered eligible. 88. Sex Transformation expenses in connection with sex transformation will not be considered eligible. 89. Sexual Dysfunction/Impotence expenses for services, supplies or drugs related to sexual dysfunction/impotence not related to organic disease will not be considered eligible. Expenses for sex therapy will not be considered eligible. 90. Skilled Nursing Facility will not be considered eligible. 91. Stand-by Physician expenses for technical medical assistance or stand-by Physician services will not be considered eligible. 92. Sterilization expenses for the reversal of elective sterilization will not be considered eligible. Male sterilization services will not be considered eligible. 93. Substance Abuse Services (Inpatient and Outpatient) will not be considered eligible. 94. Surrogate expenses relating to a surrogate pregnancy of any person who is not covered under this Plan, including but not limited to pre-pregnancy, conception, pre-natal, childbirth and post-natal expenses, will not be considered eligible. 95. Transplant expenses for services, supplies or drugs related to all organ or tissue transplant services, will not be considered eligible. Expenses for donor, transportation or travel will not be considered eligible. 96. Travel expenses for travel will not be considered eligible. 97. War expenses for the treatment of Illness or Injury resulting from a war or any act of war or terrorism, whether declared or undeclared, civil war, hostilities or invasion, or while in the armed forces of any country or international organization will not be considered eligible. 98. Weekend Admissions expenses for care and treatment billed by a Hospital for non-Medical Emergency admissions on a Friday or Saturday will not be considered eligible. 99. Wig after Chemotherapy will not be considered eligible. 100. Worker’s Compensation expenses for or in connection with any Injury or Illness which arises out of or in the course of any occupation for which the Covered Person would be entitled to compensation under any Worker’s Compensation Law or occupational disease law or similar legislation will not be considered eligible. 101. Unrelated Claims: 102. Claims for disability resulting from reversal of sterilization 103. Recreational or diversional therapy 104. Claims for temporomandibular joint syndrome 105. Routine eye care (Adult) 106. Rehabilitative therapies a. Pregnancy Benefits, including office visits and childbirth/delivery professional and facility services. b. waiting_period_sickness.v: Waiting Period : There is a 30-day waiting period to use any services besides Virtual Medical Services and Pharmacy, as detailed in the Summary of Benefits; this applies to your first year only. Additionally, the 30-day waiting does not apply to emergent care benefits included in the plan. Members that disenroll in the plan for longer than 90 days will be subject to the 30-Day waiting period. At no time will benefits reset during a 12-month enrollment.
